See Mareto in action

A guided walk through how Mareto works for community service organizations: intake, case management, reporting and the programs in between.

7 screens, about 2 minutes.
Every screen you see is configured to how your organization works.

Step 1 of 7

Your daily dashboard

The first thing staff see when they log in: a live snapshot of people, cases and activity across every program.

1
Quick actionsCreate a person, case, intake, event, appointment or announcement from the home screen. Staff never navigate away to start a record.
2
Live overview tilesPeople served, active cases, events logged, intakes, referrals and surveys, updated as staff work. Your organization picks what shows here.
3
Service area breakdownHow your clients spread across service areas. Dashboard charts are configured to any dimension you track: demographics, referral sources, risk levels.
4
AnnouncementsPriority notices every staff member sees on login: funder deadlines, policy changes, referral reminders.
5
NavigationEvery module one click away. The sidebar is configured to your organization during setup, so staff only see what they need.

  2. 2Live overview tiles. People served, active cases, events logged, intakes, referrals and surveys, updated as staff work. Your organization picks what shows here.
  3. 3Service area breakdown. How your clients spread across service areas. Dashboard charts are configured to any dimension you track: demographics, referral sources, risk levels.
  4. 4Announcements. Priority notices every staff member sees on login: funder deadlines, policy changes, referral reminders.
  5. 5Navigation. Every module one click away. The sidebar is configured to your organization during setup, so staff only see what they need.
KPI tiles are computed from the notes staff already write.In a four-program family-services build, direct, collateral and indirect hours appear on the landing page without anyone typing them.

Role-based views

Each role sees a different dashboard: frontline workers, supervisors and directors each get what is relevant to them.

Computed, not typed

Direct, collateral and indirect service hours appear on the tiles from the notes staff already write.

Always current

Numbers update as staff work. No end-of-week exports, no manual reconciliation.

Configured for you: This dashboard is built around your organization's programs, KPIs and reporting needs. Every tile, chart and announcement is specific to how you operate.

Step 2 of 7

One person, one record

Every individual has a single record no matter how many programs they touch. No duplicates, no silos.

1
One person, one recordEvery individual has exactly one record across every program. The system prompts staff to search before creating, so duplicates are prevented from day one.
2
Search and addFind anyone by name, date of birth or phone, across programs they left years ago. Export to CSV at any time: your data is yours.
3
Configurable columnsEvery column is configurable: role types, demographic fields, identity tracking, all set during implementation to match your terminology.
  1. 1One person, one record. Every individual has exactly one record across every program. The system prompts staff to search before creating, so duplicates are prevented from day one.
  2. 2Search and add. Find anyone by name, date of birth or phone, across programs they left years ago. Export to CSV at any time: your data is yours.
  3. 3Configurable columns. Every column is configurable: role types, demographic fields, identity tracking, all set during implementation to match your terminology.
One record per person, one linked family, across every program.The largest live build runs 19 programs on one person registry. Duplicate prevention at creation plus file merging when history has to be consolidated.

One linked family

A parent in the food bank and their child in the youth program are one connected family, not two strangers in two lists.

Privacy by design

Sensitive fields are masked per role. A supervisor sees different data than a case worker, automatically.

Export any time

CSV export of your whole data model at no cost. No exit fees, no lock-in.

Configured for you: The fields, roles and visibility rules on every person record are set during implementation to match your intake forms and privacy requirements.

Step 3 of 7

Case management

Every case across every program at a glance, organized by status, assigned worker and program.

1
Dashboard cardsPin the metrics that matter to the top of any page: caseload by worker, cases needing attention, closures this month.
2
Create a caseOne-click case creation linked to an existing person. The case inherits the person's details; nothing is re-entered.
3
Cases by statusOpen, pending, on hold, transferred, closed: see where every case stands without opening a record. Columns match your workflow.
  1. 1Dashboard cards. Pin the metrics that matter to the top of any page: caseload by worker, cases needing attention, closures this month.
  2. 2Create a case. One-click case creation linked to an existing person. The case inherits the person's details; nothing is re-entered.
  3. 3Cases by status. Open, pending, on hold, transferred, closed: see where every case stands without opening a record. Columns match your workflow.
One case per program enrolment; the largest build runs 19 programs on one registry.Program isolation is proven live: a counsellor in one program cannot open, or be shown, another program's file.

One case per enrolment

A person enrolled in two programs has two cases and one record. Each program sees its own file; the history stays whole.

Program fences

A note filed against another program's family is refused with the draft kept, so nothing crosses a line by accident.

Caseload in three bands

Overdue, due now, upcoming. Workers see what needs them today, not a sorted table of everything.

Configured for you: The status columns, alert thresholds and program categories are configured to your case management workflow, not a generic template.

Step 4 of 7

The event log

Every interaction, session and touchpoint in one timeline: meetings, case notes, group sessions, crisis interventions, clinical notes.

1
Tabbed views with access rulesEvents are organized into tabs: general records, group sessions, crisis interventions, clinical notes. Each tab has its own access rules; clinical notes can be restricted to their author.
2
Every interaction, loggedHome visits, phone calls, meetings, decisions: captured with person, type, date, duration and worker. Time tracking feeds service-hour reporting; no separate timesheets.
  1. 1Tabbed views with access rules. Events are organized into tabs: general records, group sessions, crisis interventions, clinical notes. Each tab has its own access rules; clinical notes can be restricted to their author.
  2. 2Every interaction, logged. Home visits, phone calls, meetings, decisions: captured with person, type, date, duration and worker. Time tracking feeds service-hour reporting; no separate timesheets.
One timeline for every interaction.The largest build carries 411 fields on a single event module across twelve programs; the form only shows the fields that apply to the event type chosen.

Replaces paper and spreadsheets

No more case notes scattered across email, paper files and shared drives. Every interaction is logged once, in one place.

Time tracking built in

Start and end times, duration and event type are captured with the note and feed service-hour reporting.

Searchable history

Find any interaction by person, type, date or worker. A complete trail for accreditation and audits.

Configured for you: Your event types, categories and access rules are defined during implementation. The system captures what your funders and accreditors require as a by-product of the work staff already do.

Step 5 of 7

Intake and referrals

Track every referral from first contact to case assignment, with full visibility into where each intake stands and where it came from.

1
Intake at a glanceClosed intakes, referral-source mix and the in-process count. Know where referrals come from and how fast you process them.
2
Create or receive intakesStart an intake in one click, or receive it through a public web form. When approved, an intake becomes a case in one click, carrying everything forward.
  1. 1Intake at a glance. Closed intakes, referral-source mix and the in-process count. Know where referrals come from and how fast you process them.
  2. 2Create or receive intakes. Start an intake in one click, or receive it through a public web form. When approved, an intake becomes a case in one click, carrying everything forward.
Public referral forms feed the record directly.A four-program family-services build runs four live referral doors, one per program, with consent state shown on the record: expired, or expiring within 60 days.

Public web forms

Referral sources submit through a form on your site and the data lands in the system. No retyping.

Intake analytics

Referral mix, processing times and waitlist depth: what funders ask for and managers need.

Intake to case

An approved intake converts to a case in one click. No duplicate entry.

Configured for you: Your referral sources, intake statuses, required fields and waitlist rules are set to match your intake process, whether that is a single point of entry or program-specific pathways.

Step 6 of 7

Reporting

Funder-ready numbers from your live data, filtered by any field, with every figure traceable to a record.

1
Filter by anythingAny field you capture is a filter: program, period, demographics, status. Anything in, anything out.
2
Automatic KPIsPeople served, cases, events, service hours, risk flags: calculated from what staff enter daily. Every number traces back to a record.
3
Download for the funderExport the filtered result as CSV or an image for the submission. No manual counting, no Excel assembly.
  1. 1Filter by anything. Any field you capture is a filter: program, period, demographics, status. Anything in, anything out.
  2. 2Automatic KPIs. People served, cases, events, service hours, risk flags: calculated from what staff enter daily. Every number traces back to a record.
  3. 3Download for the funder. Export the filtered result as CSV or an image for the submission. No manual counting, no Excel assembly.
Anything in, anything out.Buyers on demo calls describe weeks of manual assembly across three or four systems. In Mareto the funder number is a filter and a download, one number per person.

Rollup reports

One report rolls every program up for a monthly funder requirement, and each program still gets its own numbers.

Reconcilable

Figures are deterministically reconcilable: a funder can ask for the list behind a number and get it.

Any reporting period

Monthly, quarterly, annual, or a custom range. Compare periods to show trends.

Configured for you: Your report sections, KPIs and metrics are built around what your funders require. If a funder changes its template, we update the report, not your workflows.

Step 7 of 7

Many programs, one platform

Run every program from one platform, each with its own caseload, workflows and reporting, all sharing one person registry.

1
Cross-program viewHow caseloads spread across your programs: where capacity is going and which programs are busiest.
2
Program pagesEach program has its own page with dashboards, cases and reporting. Open Family Support, Youth Services, Counselling or any program to drill down.
  1. 1Cross-program view. How caseloads spread across your programs: where capacity is going and which programs are busiest.
  2. 2Program pages. Each program has its own page with dashboards, cases and reporting. Open Family Support, Youth Services, Counselling or any program to drill down.
Each program has its own forms, workflows and roles.Builds range from a two-seat single program to 19 programs and 85 seats on one platform. Nine or more programs go live in waves rather than one cutover.

Add a program without starting over

A new program is new forms, fields, workflows and roles on the same registry, not a new system.

Shared client records

When a family moves between programs, their history follows them. No re-intake, no lost information.

Grows without breaking the data model

Most of what feels like a new feature is a vocabulary entry: in the largest build 220 of 301 modules are taxonomy.

Configured for you: Each program in Mareto has its own forms, fields, workflows and role permissions, configured to how that program operates. Add programs as your organization grows.

Software is the easy part. We sort out the rest with you.

Every Mareto build starts with your impact model. We sit down with your team and work out the logic model, the referral pathways, the automations and the reporting, then configure the system to match. Our team comes from social impact, program evaluation and systems planning, and we hold your hand from discovery to go-live and after.
